anomalies.obs: On the 'Main Pump' sub-block (sheet 1, bottom), the gate of the low-side N-MOSFET T1 (IRLR2905) is pulled up to +3V3 through R26 (10 k). The only device that can pull this node low is the NPN level-shifter T5 (BT3904), whose collector also meets the gate node, plus the MCU drive via R7. With no active low drive (MCU pin high-impedance at power-on/reset, and T5 off), R26 holds the gate at +3V3 and T1 turns ON, energising the main circulation pump by default. The parallel 'ATO Valve' driver uses the opposite convention (R38 10 k pulls the gate to GND, so the valve is OFF at boot), confirming the intended topology is a default-off low-side switch.
anomalies.expected: The gate pull resistor should be tied to GND (a pull-down), as on the ATO-valve channel, so the pump MOSFET stays OFF whenever the MCU pin is floating/low (boot, reset, GPIO not yet configured). Spec §2 describes T2/IRLR2905 as a 'Main circulation-pump low-side switch ... gate driven through R1 (100 Ω) from the ESP32 pin, pre-driven via T1 (BT3904)', i.e. an active, normally-off switch.

evidence.quote: MAIN PUMP & VALVE DRIVERS / Main Pump: '+3V3' arrow above R26 10k, R26 bottom to the gate node of T1 IRLR2905 (sheet 1, row E)
ATO Valve: R38 10k from gate node of T4 AO3400A to GND (sheet 1, row E) — default-off convention
T2 — IRLR2905 (DPAK N-MOSFET) | Main circulation-pump low-side switch | ... gate driven through R1 (100 Ω) from the ESP32 pin, pre-driven via T1 (BT3904 NPN level shifter).

anomalies.impact: The main circulation pump is energised by default at power-up and during MCU reset/boot (before the GPIO is driven), and the firmware's active-high 'on' command is inverted relative to the valve channel. This can cause unintended pumping / dry-run / overflow on every reboot and makes the pump behave opposite to the intended normally-off switch.

parsed.summary: The board is largely consistent with the spec, but the main-pump MOSFET gate is pulled up to +3V3 via R26 (whereas the ATO-valve gate is pulled down to GND via R38), making the circulation pump turn ON by default at boot/reset instead of behaving as the intended normally-off low-side switch.
